name: Daphni
label: Jiaolong
lede: A maths PhD, a punk singer's lawyers, a Polaris Prize and a label of his own: the dancefloor side of Dan Snaith, who is also Caribou and was Manitoba.

eras.title: A maths student called Manitoba
eras.text: Before Daphni, before Caribou, Dan Snaith was Manitoba: bedroom electronics on Leaf, made while he worked toward a doctorate in mathematics. It ended when a punk singer's lawyers took an interest in the name.

years.h: People Eating Fruit: the first Manitoba EP
years.p: [[Dan Snaith|20ffdffa-9e17-4968-98ca-3434064b00bb]] starts releasing music as Manitoba with the EP People Eating Fruit, a year before his first album.

years.h: Start Breaking My Heart · Leaf
years.p: Snaith's debut album as Manitoba, on The Leaf Label, gets compared to Boards of Canada, [[Four Tet|3bcff06f-675a-451f-9075-99e8657047e8]] and Aphex Twin.
years.xp:
Pitchfork first scored it 8.0, then revised that to 7.9 in 2006. In 2017 the site put it at No. 40 on its list of the 50 best IDM albums of all time.

It was reissued in 2006 by Domino, after Snaith had become Caribou.

years.h: Up in Flames, the last record called Manitoba
years.p: Snaith's second album on Leaf is the final one released under the Manitoba name.

years.cap: Dan Snaith in his early years
years.src: Wikipedia: Richard Manitoba · Wikipedia: Dan Snaith
years.h: Handsome Dick Manitoba threatens to sue, so Manitoba becomes Caribou
years.p: Richard 'Handsome Dick' Manitoba of the Dictators threatened legal action over the name, and Snaith switched to Caribou rather than fight it.
years.xp: Wikipedia's page on Richard Manitoba puts it in a single sentence: in 2004 he threatened to sue Snaith for using the band name, and Snaith changed his name to Caribou. The Manitoba albums were reissued under the new name.

eras.title: Caribou, and a doctorate on the side
eras.text: The new name comes with a new sound: psychedelic pop, then a record built for the dancefloor. Snaith picks up a PhD, a Polaris Prize and a long-running live band along the way.

years.h: Snaith finishes a maths PhD at Imperial College London
years.p: His doctorate, supervised by Kevin Buzzard, is on overconvergent Siegel modular symbols. His father Victor and sister Nina are mathematicians too.
years.xp: Snaith has described the thesis himself: 'original, but I would still call it trivial.'

years.big: Read it off the back of a milk truck
years.src: Wikipedia: The Milk of Human Kindness
years.h: First record as Caribou: The Milk of Human Kindness
years.p: Snaith's own answer, per Wikipedia, to where he found the title; the line it echoes is Shakespeare's, from Macbeth.
years.xp: It came out on Leaf and Domino and was Snaith's first record under the Caribou name. Pitchfork gave it 8.5. Producer Ryan Lewis later sampled 'Subotnick' for a 2009 project with Macklemore.

years.h: Andorra goes psychedelic pop
years.p: Released on City Slang in the UK and Merge in the US, with 'Melody Day' as the lead single.
years.xp: Uncut called the lead single the most striking result of Snaith's immersion in psychedelic soft-pop. Pitchfork's Mark Richardson reviewed the record on August 23, 2007.

years.h: Andorra wins the Polaris Music Prize
years.p: A record Snaith made after a maths doctorate takes Canada's album-of-the-year prize for 2008.

years.src: Wikipedia: Swim (Caribou album) · The Quietus: Modular Love
years.h: Swim: 700 tracks down to nine
years.p: Snaith says he just got up every day wanting to make music; he ended up with roughly 700 tracks and picked nine.
years.xp:
Nights DJing at London's Plastic People pushed him toward the dancefloor. Snaith told The Quietus he saw Theo Parrish play there and made 'Bowls' within days; he was already thinking about Daphni, he said, because 'there was stuff that needed another outlet.'

Pitchfork gave Swim 8.4 and later put it on its 2014 list of the 100 best albums of the decade so far. Resident Advisor named it album of 2010. 'Odessa' turned up in FIFA 11 and in ads for Lexus and Tissot.

eras.title: Daphni: the dancefloor alias
eras.text: Daphni starts as a place for tracks that don't fit a Caribou record: quick, loop-based, made for the next DJ set. Snaith releases them on his own Jiaolong label, then keeps the Caribou machine running alongside.

years.src: Various Small Flames: Four Tet/Daphni · Wikipedia: Daphni (musician)
years.h: Daphni debuts on a split with Four Tet
years.p: 'Ye Ye' appears on a 12-inch on [[Four Tet|3bcff06f-675a-451f-9075-99e8657047e8]]'s Text label, with Kieran Hebden taking the flip with 'Pinnacles'.
years.xp: Various Small Flames called it another pseudonym of Caribou's Dan Snaith. The same month came Daphni Edits Vol. 1 on Resista, followed by Vol. 2 in August.

years.h: JIAOLONG001: Snaith starts his own label
years.p: Daphni's first 12-inch on Jiaolong, a label meant to put records out with as little fuss as possible.
years.xp: XLR8R reports he built the label so tracks could arrive and disappear from shops the way dance records do. 'Daphni' is Greek for bay leaf; Snaith picked it for its femininity and organic quality, per the same piece.

years.src: The Quietus: Modular Love · XLR8R: Deep Inside: Daphni 'Jiaolong' · Wikipedia: Jiaolong (album)
yt: Daphni Boiler Room London DJ set
years.h: Jiaolong, nine tracks and a custom modular
years.p: The first Daphni album collects five earlier singles and four new tracks, most of them made on a modular synth Snaith built himself.
years.xp:
'Each of the tracks on the record was made in a day,' Snaith told The Quietus. He says the modular 'doesn't allow you the possibility of going back and second guessing yourself.'

Metacritic collected 76; NME and Spin each gave it 8/10. It made the 2013 Polaris longlist.

q: The whole idea is it's not just me, and it's not just hired guns.
years.h: Caribou supports Radiohead on the King of Limbs tour
years.p: Snaith's live Caribou band, with Ryan Smith, Brad Weber and later John Schmersal, plays support dates for Radiohead.
years.xp: Snaith says the live show is its own thing, with a proper band in which everyone is equally part of it. Smith has played with him since 2003, Weber since 2007 and Schmersal since 2009.

years.h: Julia / Tiberius: a Daphni 12-inch with Owen Pallett
years.p: [[Owen Pallett|6d394418-a565-4c16-9dec-f5a89e213cde]] is credited on the Jiaolong single.

years.src: Wikipedia: Our Love (Caribou album) · Wikipedia: Dan Snaith
years.h: Our Love, written after his daughter's birth
years.p: Snaith makes a more personal record, with [[Jessy Lanza|0dfb3c3d-e140-4575-baf3-7ff20ae56c9c]] and Owen Pallett on some tracks; Pitchfork tagged it Best New Music.
years.xp: It came out on City Slang, with Merge releasing it the next day. It was nominated for a Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album, made the 2015 Polaris shortlist and won the IMPALA Album of the Year award.

eras.title: A mix, a mixtape, a voice
eras.text: Daphni gets a proper DJ mix and a second album, and Snaith puts his own voice at the front of the next Caribou record.

years.h: FabricLive.93: 27 tracks in an hour and 13 minutes
years.p: Snaith's Fabric mix lands as Daphni, with tracks by Luther Davis Group, Pheeroan akLaff and Container.

years.h: Joli Mai, the second Daphni album
years.p: Twelve tracks, 59 minutes, put out on his own Jiaolong label, with some material drawn from the Fabric mix.
years.xp: Metacritic collected 78. It placed No. 10 on Exclaim!'s 2017 dance/electronic list and No. 5 on Rolling Stone's 20 best EDM/electronic albums of 2017.

years.h: The Sizzling EP
years.p: A Daphni EP with a title track that also came out as a single.

years.h: Suddenly: 900 ideas, 12 tracks
years.p: Snaith names it after a word his daughter was obsessed with; Pitchfork gave it 8.2.
years.xp: It won the 2021 Juno for Electronic Album of the Year and made the Polaris shortlist. The singles were 'Home', 'You and I' and 'Never Come Back'.

eras.title: Cherry
eras.text: Five years after Joli Mai, the third Daphni album arrives. Pitchfork scores it 8.2 and puts it at No. 25 on its best albums of 2022.

years.src: Resident Advisor: Daphni - Cherry · Consequence: Caribou's Dan Snaith announces new Daphni album Cherry
years.h: 'Cherry' arrives first, then 'Cloudy' and 'Mania'
years.p: The title track is a DX7 and a bassline that spirals out, per Resident Advisor; 'Cloudy' follows in June with the album announcement.
years.xp: Resident Advisor's single review heard a three-note motif mid-track bent and warmed-over like the melodies on old Manitoba records. Snaith called the essence of 'Cloudy' keeping it aloft, like nudging a balloon that's only just heavier than air.

q: The most fun there is to be had on a dance record this year.
years.src: Wikipedia: Cherry (Daphni album) · Album of the Year: Daphni - Cherry
years.h: Cherry: Pitchfork gives it 8.2 and ranks it No. 25 of 2022
years.p: Fourteen tracks, 47 minutes, recorded at Metropolis Studio in London and released on Jiaolong.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Sherburne called it 'a tour de force of dancefloor intuition and emotional release.' Metacritic gave it 82 from eight reviews; AllMusic picked it among its electronic albums of the year, and The Atlantic ranked it No. 4 of 2022. Matt Colton mastered it.

eras.title: Back to Caribou, then back to Daphni
eras.text: A big dancefloor Caribou record, and then a fourth Daphni album that makes the Polaris longlist.

years.h: Honey, big dancefloor Caribou
years.p: 'Volume' samples MARRS' 'Pump Up the Volume'; Pitchfork gave the record 7.8, Metacritic 73.
years.xp: Snaith said he wanted 'huge dancefloor tracks' and to keep the thrill when something hits really hard. It made the 2025 Polaris longlist.

years.h: Butterfly, the fourth Daphni album, makes the Polaris longlist
years.p: Wikipedia also lists an expanded edition with seven new tracks and remixes for September 2026.
